steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Cut bread into 1-inch cubes. Transfer to a baking sheet and spread in a single layer.
Toast in the preheated oven, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned, 8 to 10 minutes. Remove from the oven.
Beat sugar, butter, milk, and eggs in a large bowl until well combined. Stir in undrained pineapple and toasted bread; toss until coated. Pour mixture into the prepared baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until puffed and golden, about 45 minutes.
Serve warm with a sprinkle of powdered sugar.

raw_recipe.headline: Scalloped Pineapple

review.reviewBody:
**EDIT** i made this again and realized that the first time i made it I accidently used only one stick of butter instead of the 2 (1 Cup) it calls for. 2 sticks of butter was too much and made it oily and greasy. 1 stick or 1/2 cup of melted butter was plenty. I also prefer using crushed pinapple instead of chunks.**

Delicious! I used 1 C whipping cream instead of milk, brown sugar instead of white and added raisins and cinnamon.

I love this dish, and serve it to my B&B guests for breakfast. However, after baking it the original way many times, I have found you can do the following with equally good results and not so many calories: replace 1 C butter with 1/4 C butter and 3/4 C low fat buttermilk; I use plain almond milk (no sugar) for the milk, and use 1 C sugar rather than 2 cups. With these changes you've eliminated >500 calories by replacing the butter and 775 calories by eliminating a cup of sugar. The dish is still sweet and you don't have to feel so guilty about eating it. Oh, I did increase the bread by 3-4 slices to soak up the extra buttermilk. Enjoy!

Making the recipe "as is" I gave this dish 4 stars. To make it 5 stars, I made the following changes:
1.) I used about 1/2 loaf of Italian bread. The "crust" pieces are really delish. I took the dish I was going to bake this in & then tore pieces to kinda fill the pan. If you don't have enough bread it can be too "wet".
2.) Use 4 eggs
3.) Add 1 Tbls vanilla
4.) Only use 3/4 cup sugar, it will be plenty sweet.
5.) Use 20 oz. can CRUSHED Pineapple, untrained.

I don't know what happened, but I had WAY too much liquid. Maybe I used the wrong type of bread. I used Sarah Lee Atesano bread and maybe it just didn't need that much liquid. Anyway I drained off the extra liquid before cooking, just eye-balling it, and it turned out great.
just a few changes to suit our tastes .. I used finely chopped fresh pineapple, 1/2 the sugar , added 1 tsp cinnamon, and the best part ..added 1/2 pack of cream cheese chunked. yummy

thanks for reviewing my recipe; great ideas! i never really thought about adding anything to it, i love it so much the way it is. i think that if you make it with whipping cream it will add too much more fat to keep the butter content at one cup, too. the one thing i do to this recipe that VASTLY improves on it is make homemade wheat bread with stone ground wheat flour and use that for the toast. thanks for the pic too!

I made this for a church Potluck Fellowship Lunch. I thought this sounded delicious but being that it's December (just after Thanksgiving) I added a cup of fresh cranberry's to the originial recipe. IT WAS AWESOME!!! Everyone that tasted it loved it and wanted the recipe! Thanks so much for this recipe. I will definitely make this again and again!

I had this growing up. I had a aunt that use to make it. Her recipe was never wrote down. So was very happy to see your recipe. I did some changing to it. I used a 1/2 cup of Splenda and used French bread
My family loved this recipe! ! I used pinapple tidbits, sooooo good no matter what pinapple you use ( ive used them all). I did cut the sugar in half (preference). But Awesome!!

I used Italian bread for this recipe and it was fantastic!! My mom said it was even better than what my Great-grandmother made and that was pretty great!! I made it for Thanksgiving and I am making it for Christmas dinner too!! My husband loved it!! Toasting the bread makes a big difference, it keeps the casserole from being soggy!! Soooo Good!

I have to say, this was awesome. Next time I will try splenda instead of all the sugar. It was very sweet...If your diabetic do not eat! I will be making this again I'm sure. Family loved it. I wanted to take some for work but it never made it out of the house. Thanks!

MUST MODIFY...original recipe has way too much sugar so I modified it by cutting sugar to 1 cup....2 cups will make it unnecessarily sweet! For the milk, I used 1/2c almond milk with a 1/4c of dairy free caramel creamer. It was absolutely delicious! Great with a cup of coffee!! :)

I followed the recipe except I made two of the recommended changes by other reviewers. I cut the sugar in half and added a touch of vanilla. It was plenty sweet and had good flavor. But the consistency is very unpleasant. I thought perhaps I had undercooked it so I returned it to the oven for an extra fifteen minutes. That did nothing to improve the consistency. It's like eating wet undercooked eggs. I was embarrassed to serve it to my guests. They were polite but didn't accept seconds.
I made this just as it is written. We loved it. I plan on making it for our annual fall party this weekend.
This is so good, and very easy to make! I added some baking chocolate on top after taking it out of the oven

I make this recipe all the time and absolutely love it. I don't sprinkle the powdered sugar over the top, but other than that, I make this recipe exactly as originally written. If there is any left over, it actually even freezes well, so I freeze in single-size servings and it's perfect to have on hand for the times you bring home a doggie bag from a restaurant, but it's not quite enough to fill you up--add your single serving of this pineapple dish and you then have a wonderful meal.
very easy and very good
Made it for Christmas dinner. It was very sweet. Had a nice flavor, but was more like a dessert than a side dish with ham. My family didn't really care for it. I probably won't be making it again.
This recipe is great. Had it with grilled ham steaks and it was the perfect side. will definitely make often!

My husband and I did not like this at all, everything about it was totally unappealing from the way it looked, smelled, tasted and even the texture. Obviously the other reviewers enjoyed it so I guess there are some people out there who like this sort of thing. Not us.
